title: decompose-worklet-scheduler-and-stabilize-kv-prefetch
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Summary: Break the monolithic worklet scheduler into a small set of focused components (admission, placement, lifecycle) and harden the KV prefetch path to eliminate intermittent cache stalls under mixed workloads. This ticket consolidates multiple smaller hacks added during peak growth: a shared token lock in the scheduler, fragile prefetch backoff heuristics, and an uninstrumented hotset sampler. Goals:
- Decompose scheduler into WorkletAdmission, WorkletPlacement, and WorkletReaper with well-defined interfaces so future optimizations (work stealing, preemption) are pluggable.
- Replace global token lock with per-shard admission queues and optimistic fast-path for common-case enqueues.
- Stabilize KV prefetch: remove exponential backoff that overshoots on cold starts, add an adaptive rate limiter informed by recent miss ratio, and make prefetch CircuitBreaker observable.
- Add end-to-end metrics: queue depth histograms per shard, admission latency p50/p95/p99, prefetch success ratio, kv-prefetch-triggered-cpu-ms.
Acceptance criteria:
1) No increase in median generation latency for 95% of requests; p95 latency must not regress more than 5ms on our canary traffic compared to baseline.
2) KV cache miss bursts reduced by >= 30% on the mixed (chat+completion) workload in the replay test.
3) Scheduler unit tests for edge conditions (shutdown, preemption, backpressure) added and flake rate on CI < 0.5%.
4) New metrics are emitted and surfaced in Console dashboards (token-level traces optional) and correlate with reduced CPU/cold-miss incidents.
Implementation notes:
- Start by refactoring the scheduler package to extract interfaces and a thin coordination layer; keep behavioral compatibility (feature flags on) to allow canary.
- Implement per-shard admission queues with bounded MPSC ring buffers. Provide a fast-path that avoids atomics when the queue is uncontended.
- Prefetch: replace the hand-rolled backoff with a leaky-bucket rate limiter keyed by model+route and a simple sliding-window miss counter to trigger extra prefetches.
- CircuitBreaker state persists to memory only and is safe to reconstruct after process restart (tolerate transient cold misses).
- Add tracing spans around admission and prefetch to enable root-cause analysis in live incidents.
Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests -> integration replay (local) -> shadow traffic in staging (72h) -> 1% production canary (48h) -> 10% ramp (48h) -> full rollout.
- Feature-flag all runtime changes with a kill-switch that reverts to the existing scheduler/prefetch behavior without restarting services.
- Run extended replay with adversarial patterns (bursty chat sessions, long-context generations) and capture CPU, latency, and kv miss telemetry.
- If p95 regression or elevated errors observed, roll back feature flag and attach diagnostic heap/profile artifacts.
Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle race between admission fast-path and shard reparenting. Mitigation: add versioning to shard handles and assert on mismatches in debug builds.
- Risk: misconfigured rate limiter could underprefetch leading to higher latency. Mitigation: conservative default limits and canary-derived thresholds; make limits dynamically tunable from Console.
